evidence.reference: manual packaged-app test of native WebView download/navigation/new-window enforcement
evidence.note: 2026-08-17. User-directed architecture change (explicit scope agreed in advance: webview + downloads + navigation, not session isolation, not permission integration). A real download (GitHub release .zip, forces Content-Disposition: attachment) was blocked and recorded in Audit. A window.open()-style request initially bypassed both on_navigation and on_download entirely (wry's default behavior) until on_new_window was added to deny it. Positioning verified correct at default window size and after resize/maximize. Known, documented limitation: content a site renders inline instead of forcing a download (e.g. Wikipedia's PDF export, via WebKit's built-in PDF viewer) is not caught, since on_navigation only checks URL scheme, not response content type -- confirmed no fix is possible with Tauri's current public API (on_web_resource_request is documented as tauri-protocol-only, not applicable to external URLs).

evidence.reference: manual packaged-app test of real per-profile WKWebsiteDataStore isolation
evidence.note: 2026-08-17. User-directed, scope expanded beyond the original recommendation (persistent profiles only) to full isolation for all profiles once wry 0.55.1 (already pinned) was confirmed to expose remove_data_store directly. Three real bugs found only by running the packaged app (none visible from cargo check/test): a removal/teardown race ('data store is currently opened'), a fixed webview label causing the previous profile's content to keep showing after switching, and scroll desync from only listening to ResizeObserver. All three fixed and reverified. Direct proof of isolation: switching from Medical (real Google search state) to Financial showed a fresh, unauthenticated Google homepage. Confirmed via a throwaway Rust probe reading the encrypted database directly that profile_data_stores persists correctly and audit events record each open/remove.

next_action.description: No specific outstanding action. All profiles now have real per-profile WKWebsiteDataStore isolation (macOS/iOS only), with genuine wipe-on-close for ephemeral profiles. A user-suggested future idea, not scoped or started: per-profile content filtering/customization based on each profile's policy parameters. The 'WebView Decision Log' duplicate-entries observation from the 2026-08-17 packaged revalidation remains separately unconfirmed as a real defect.

summary: Privacy-focused Tauri browser shell with passing automated validation and a canonical human-verified packaged macOS WebView validation covering HTTPS-only navigation, blocked HTTP navigation and downloads, sandboxing, policy badges, and decision logging. This cycle fixed several silent-failure and correctness bugs (unhandled Tauri command errors, an isolation-scope cleanup leak, a disconnected vault bookmark count), corrected UI/audit-log claims that overstated session isolation as real per-profile cookie/storage separation, replaced the encrypted-export passphrase key derivation with salted Argon2id, moved the permission and download decision registries from in-memory-only to SQLite persistence, added SQLCipher at-rest encryption for the live database with the key stored in the OS keychain, and -- at the user's explicit direction, with scope agreed in advance -- migrated the live WebView from an iframe to a real native child webview with genuine Rust-enforced download and navigation policy, then went further to give every profile its own real WKWebsiteDataStore with genuine wipe-on-close for ephemeral profiles. Permission-callback integration and inline-content-type download detection remain blocked on gaps in Tauri's current public API, not oversight.
current_objective: Keep the validated packaged WebView privacy boundary honest: fix concrete bugs and false claims as found. Architecture expansion happens only at explicit user direction with scope agreed in advance, not proactively.
known_gaps: Per-profile storage isolation only applies on macOS/iOS (data_store_identifier is platform-specific) and only inside the packaged app, not the dev preview. Windows/Linux would need a separate data_directory-based approach, not implemented. Tracked honestly in src/app/threatModel.ts.

Permission-callback integration (camera/mic/geolocation) is not implemented -- wry 0.56.0 added the underlying PermissionKind/PermissionResponse API, but tauri (pinned and latest-published at 2.11.5) hasn't wrapped it in WebviewBuilder yet.

Content a site renders inline instead of forcing a download (e.g. a PDF export handled by the WebView's built-in viewer) is not caught by download blocking -- on_navigation only checks URL scheme, not response content type, and Tauri's on_web_resource_request is documented as tauri-protocol-only, not applicable to external URLs. No fix possible with the current public API.
Per-profile content filtering/customization (restricting what's allowed/displayed based on each profile's own policy parameters) -- a user-suggested future idea, not scoped or started.
constraints: Do not add a new browser subsystem or expand architecture proactively -- only at explicit user direction, with scope agreed in advance (see the 2026-08-17 native WebView migration for the pattern: user asked to resolve a specific blocked item, scope was confirmed via options before implementation started).
Do not weaken download blocking or permission prompting.
Do not treat smoke tests as proof of packaged desktop behavior.
Manual validation must use bounded, non-sensitive test URLs and content.
Do not let UI copy, audit events, or the threat model claim privacy guarantees (e.g. storage isolation) that aren't actually implemented.
